sources.citation: Bennett, Ryan. 2016. Mayan phonology. Language and Linguistics Compass 10(10): 469-514.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent Ch'olti'/Cholti: no occurrence; the survey does not cover the extinct language.

sources.citation: Becquey, Cédric. 2014. Diasystème, diachronie: Études comparées dans les langues cholanes. PhD dissertation, Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam. Utrecht: LOT (LOT Dissertation Series 377), 2 vols., 1021 pp.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: §1.3.5 'Cholti'' (pp. 125-128) reconstructs 20 consonants and 5 vowels from the Morán orthography (no length contrast recoverable); says nothing about accent. §1.4 'Quelques éléments prosodiques' (pp. 129-140) covers only Ch'orti' (fixed final word accent, after Fought), Chol and modern Chontal, opening with 'La prosodie des langues cholanes est encore très peu étudiée. Seul le ch'orti'.. a fait l'objet d'une analyse systématique de ses accents lexicaux.' No statement for Ch'olti'.

sources.citation: Feldman, Lawrence H. 2007. English/Ch'oltí'/Spanish Dictionary (based on the Arte y diccionario en lengua Choltí, 1695). FAMSI online database.
sources.note: Landing page/introduction read via direct download: nothing on pronunciation, accent marks or stress.

sources.citation: Boot, Erik. 2004. Vocabulary in the Ch'olti' language: A transcription of the 'Bocabulario Grande' by Fray Francisco Morán (1695). FAMSI (Foundation for the Advancement of Mesoamerican Studies).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Introduction gives only a grapheme-to-phoneme correspondence table for Morán's orthography; no mention of stress or accent (a full-text search for stress/accent full text: no 'stress/accent/acento').

sources.citation: Sattler, Mareike. 2004. Ch'olti': An analysis of the Arte de la lengua Ch'olti by Fray Francisco Morán. In Søren Wichmann (ed.), The Linguistics of Maya Writing, 365-405. Salt Lake City: University of Utah Press.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Chapter runs Introduction -> Verbs -> Nouns -> Pronouns -> Adjectives -> Numerals -> Participles -> Prepositions -> Particles -> Conjunctions; only phonological remark is a paragraph (p. 367) on the manuscript's 'inadequate orthography, which does not reflect all sounds of Ch'olti, especially neglecting the glottal stops'. No mention of stress/accent.

sources.citation: Fought, John G. 1984. Choltí Maya: A sketch. In M. S. Edmonson (ed.), Supplement to the Handbook of Middle American Indians, vol. 2: Linguistics, pp. 43-55. Austin: University of Texas Press. ISBN 0-292-77577-6.

sources.note: Only dedicated synchronic sketch of Ch'olti' by a phonologist (author of the Ch'orti' stress analyses); if any modern source states or infers Ch'olti' accent placement from the Morán MS, it is this one.
